ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, quadrilateral ABCD has drawn a dashed diagonal AC from A to C; this dashed line divides the quadrilateral into two triangles ABC and ADC. Given by the problem, AB=4, BC=7, AD=5, CD=10, let AC=x. Use the strict triangle inequality for triangle ABC: |7-4|<x<7+4, so 3<x<11. Use the strict triangle inequality for triangle ADC: |10-5|<x<10+5, so 5<x<15. Taking the intersection of the two gives 5<x<11. The integer values are 6,7,8,9,10, so the count is 5.
